items.title: The ideal of denominators of a regular meromorphic section: two short exact sequences with support condition and a cycle-theoretic difference formula
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is stated for an invertible module L on a scheme X locally of finite type over a base situation, a coherent sheaf F with support all of X and no embedded associated points, X of delta-dimension at most k+1 with no embedded points, and a regular meromorphic section s; it asserts two short exact sequences starting in I F, that the cokernels Q_1, Q_2 have delta-dimension at most k, that s restricts to a regular meromorphic section on each component of dimension k+1, and that [Q_2]_k - [Q_1]_k equals both the explicit divisor sum and the cap product c_1(L) cap [F]_{k+1} in CH_k(X) (statement lines 18648-18712). The proof exhibits the two injections via the regular-section construction, gets the support bound from the nowhere dense support of the cokernels, and then reduces the cycle identity to a computation at the generic point xi of an arbitrary integral closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension k: writing s = (a/b) s_xi with a, b nonzerodivisors in A = O_{X, xi}, it identifies the coefficient of [Z] on the left as length_A(M/(a/b)IM) - length_A(M/IM) and on the right as the sum over the minimal primes q_i of A of length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) ord_{A/q_i}(a/b), then quotes the module-level lemma (proof lines 18715-18752). Recognising the coefficient computation as an instance of the module statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
